facts.raw_span: A 46-year-old Japanese woman
history of epilepsy
redness and swelling of the right breast
erythema and swelling in the lower right breast
Ultrasound revealed a 54 × 41 × 31 mm low-echo mass with partially unclear margins in the outer right breast
invasive ductal carcinoma (no special type), high grade, ER+, PgR–, HER2 3+, Ki67 70%
Whole-body PET-CT revealed increased uptake in the right axilla, anterior mediastinum, left pleura, and liver
consistent with cT4dN3M1 stage IV breast cancer
lesions nearly disappeared
clinical complete response maintained for 23 months
persistent headache
a 30-mm mass lesion in the right temporal lobe

concepts.why: The patient has a history of invasive ductal carcinoma and stage IV breast cancer.
The patient developed a mass lesion in the right temporal lobe after treatment for breast cancer.
The patient has a history of epilepsy.
The patient was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma.
The patient was diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer.
The patient developed a persistent headache and a mass lesion in the right temporal lobe after treatment with trastuzumab.

rationales.F02: Epilepsy is a known condition, which is being considered as a potential cause for the patient's symptoms.
rationales.F06: The presence of HER2 3+ and high Ki67 suggests an aggressive tumor, but the patient responded well to trastuzumab, making trastuzumab-resistant breast cancer less likely.
rationales.F11: A persistent headache could be a symptom of brain metastasis or epilepsy.
rationales.F12: A mass lesion in the right temporal lobe is highly suggestive of brain metastasis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's persistent headache and the 30-mm mass lesion in the right temporal lobe are highly specific findings that support brain metastasis, which is a known complication of breast cancer.
